title: Senior Director, Engine & Plant Solutions Strategy
text:
**Job Description**
===================

This role defines how the GE Vernova Gas Power portfolio should evolve over a 5-year horizon and leads the front end of the hardware portfolio and NPI funnel. The leader converts shifts in customer needs, energy markets, technology, policy, competition, and adjacent value pools into an integrated portfolio architecture, prioritized opportunity pipeline, and decision-ready investment recommendations across heavy-duty gas turbines, aeroderivative gas turbines, steam turbines, generators, heat-recovery and balance-of-plant systems, equipment controls, and integrated engine and plant architectures.

 
 

The role matures outyear hardware and engine-solution opportunities until customer value, strategic fit, architecture, technical feasibility, economics, risk, ownership, and execution pathways are sufficiently defined for a Product Management decision. At that point, accountability transitions through a formal tollgate to Product Management, which owns funded commercialization, product roadmap execution, lifecycle performance, quality, delivery, and product cost.

 
 

Expected to work in a high intensity, sprint-based model, with high exposure to Power SLT on business-defining recommendations.

 
 

**Scope boundaries within the Strategy & Product Management team**
------------------------------------------------------------------

**Joint seams:** Data centers, distributed generation, hybrid systems and other cross-portfolio opportunities require a named lead by value proposition. This role leads when the core question is engine, equipment, controls or plant architecture; Software & Services Strategy leads when the core question is digital/services value capture; New Business Industrialization leads when the opportunity requires venture incubation or formation of a new business.

**Owned by New Business Industrialization:** Startup-like opportunities, external or emerging technologies requiring venture-style incubation, new business models, sandbox or stand-alone operating structures, early commercialization, and industrialization pathways outside the established hardware portfolio. This role may identify or sponsor a signal, but transfers venture incubation accountability.

**Owned by Software & Services Strategy:** Software products, industrial data and AI, digital platforms, recurring-revenue models, software-enabled services, services transformation, installed-base service strategy, and the enterprise value proposition that combines software, controls and services. This role supplies hardware and controls-interface requirements but does not own that strategy.

**Owned by this role:** Long-range hardware portfolio architecture; heavy-duty and aeroderivative engine platforms; steam, generator and balance-of-plant hardware; equipment controls and controls interfaces; new centerlines and derivatives; physical plant and power-island architectures; hardware competitiveness; and transition of defined opportunities into Product Management/NPI.

 
 

**Organizational scope**
------------------------

* Reports directly into the VP Power Strategy, with a formal operating interlock to the head of Product Management and the Power executive leadership team.

* Leads 4-6 direct reports plus cross-functional opportunity teams formed around priority initiatives.

* Global scope across new units, installed base, services, software and controls, digital offerings, engine and plant-system solutions, and selected adjacencies.

* Owns portfolio recommendations and incubation governance, not engineering line management, product P&Ls, commercial execution, or lifecycle delivery after transition.

* Decision rights include opportunity admission, evidence requirements, incubation funding recommendations, gate-readiness certification, and stop/pivot recommendations. Final investment approvals remain with designated business governance.

 
 

Required Qualifications

 
 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, economics, finance, computer science, or a related discipline.

* Typically 15+ years of progressively responsible experience across portfolio strategy, product management, engineering, technology commercialization, services, commercial strategy, or corporate/business strategy in complex industrial markets.

* Demonstrated leadership of enterprise-scale portfolio choices, new-platform evaluations, or integrated solution development involving material investment and multi-year uncertainty.

* Deep understanding of industrial product economics, lifecycle value, R&D/NPI governance, customer buying processes, and commercialization.

* Fluency in financial modeling, scenario analysis, business cases, capital allocation, and option-based decision making.

* Evidence of leading through influence across senior stakeholders with competing incentives and no direct reporting authority.

* Exceptional written and verbal executive communication, including the ability to simplify complex technical and market choices without losing rigor.

* Ability and willingness to engage customers globally and travel as required.

 
 

For candidates applying to a U.S. based position, the pay range for this position is between $248,000 and $341,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set.

Bonus eligibility: discretionary annual bonus

This posting is expected to remain open for at least seven days after it was posted on 11/23/26.

Available benefits include medical, dental, vision, and prescription drug coverage; access to Health Coach from GE Vernova, a 24/7 nurse-based resource; and access to the Employee Assistance Program, providing 24/7 confidential assessment, counseling and referral services. Retirement benefits include the GE Vernova Retirement Savings Plan, a tax-advantaged 401(k) savings opportunity with company matching contributions and company retirement contributions, as well as access to Fidelity Executive Services. Other benefits include tuition assistance, adoption assistance, paid parental leave, disability benefits, life insurance, 12 paid holidays, and permissive time off, and the Restoration Plan, a nonqualified plan with company credits on eligible pay above IRS limits.
